subject: Real-world latency checklist and verification plan (hosted vs current provider)
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.inference.com>
To: Jordan Marks <jordan.marks@acme.ai>, Tina Xu <tina.xu@veridian.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 15:20:00 +0000
Subject: Real-world latency checklist and verification plan (hosted vs current provider)

Hi Jordan / Tina —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and an actionable checklist so we can get a side-by-side verification running next week. My objective here is to make the PoC as apples-to-apples as possible so your infra team can validate end-to-end p95/p99 under real traffic shapes.

High-level goals
- Measure real-world end-to-end latency (client-to-first-byte and client-to-last-byte) for the two flavors: Redwood hosted API vs your current provider.
- Validate streaming behavior (chunked responses + early-first-byte) and concurrency/throughput under sustained load.
- Produce simple pass/fail against your SLOs and a short report with percentile distributions + error modes.

Proposed acceptance thresholds (customer-provided targets we discussed)
- p95 end-to-end: <= 300 ms
- p99 end-to-end: <= 900 ms
- Sustained throughput target: 60 requests/sec (sustained window)
- Concurrency target: 200 concurrent active requests at peak
- Streaming: first-byte latency for streaming chunks <= 120 ms p95 (for multi-chunk responses)

What we need from Acme to run an equivalent comparison
- A 24–72 hour traffic replay file (JSONL) with representative request sizes and a simple session map; if you can’t share, a small traffic generator script and traffic envelope will do.
- Identify a production-like client region (US-east) and the IP ranges that will be running the test so we can mirror routing.
- The definitions you use for p95/p99 (start/stop timestamps): do you measure from client request send to first byte, or from client request completion? We’ll default to client-send -> first-byte and client-send -> last-byte and include both.

Redwood deliverables for the PoC
- Test harness + JMeter/Locust config to replay your traffic (we can adapt).
- Two hosted endpoints configured for the test: hosted-small (baseline) and hosted-boost (burst/throughput).
- Raw latency traces (JSONL) instrumented with x-rw-testid and x-rw-span headers for correlation.
- Aggregated report with p50/p95/p99, error rates, tail distribution, and a short tuning recommendation list.

Timing
- Proposed kickoff: Tue May 18 (setup day)
- Run window: Wed May 19 00:00 UTC — Fri May 21 00:00 UTC (48–72 hours)
- Debrief: Mon May 24 (analysis + recommendations)

Next steps (action items)
1) Jordan: send a small traffic sample (or a link to a replay) and the definitive SLO definitions by EOD Thu May 13.
2) Tina: confirm any existing middleware or edge-layer caching that we should know about (CDN, API gateway timeouts).
3) Ben / Marissa: I’ll share the checklist and a short test plan; Ben to add acceptance hooks we want instrumented on the Redwood side.

Attachments: soojin_poc-slo-checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet: traffic slices, token distributions, test schedule)

Thanks — I’ll follow up with the test endpoint details once I have the traffic sample.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Enterprise Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.inference.com
+1 (415) 555-0182

From: Jordan Marks <jordan.marks@acme.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 16:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Real-world latency checklist and verification plan (hosted vs current provider)

Thanks Soojin — this is very helpful. A couple quick clarifications from our end: 

1) Traffic replay: we can provide a 24-hour JSONL (anonymized) with session IDs and token counts. Will that be enough for you to scale to 72 hours?
2) Measurement points: we currently measure client-send -> last-byte for SLOs. We’re happy to include first-byte measurements if Redwood can provide both.
3) Streaming behavior: our product uses chunked streaming for multi-turn assistant responses. Typical payloads are: 65% single-turn (~120 tokens), 35% multi-turn (avg 520 tokens, ~3 chunks). The multi-turn flows are the ones that stress tail latency for us.

We’ll aim to get the replay file over by Thu May 13. Also looping in our infra lead, Tina, to confirm edge/network bits.

Jordan
Jordan Marks
Head of Engineering | Acme.ai
jordan.marks@acme.ai

Subject: Re: Real-world latency checklist and verification plan (hosted vs current provider)

Appreciate the quick reply, Jordan — perfect. A few clarifications and what we’ll instrument on the Redwood side: 

Traffic replay sizing
- 24-hour sample is fine to bootstrap; we’ll stretch the workload synthetically to simulate a 72-hour window while keeping the same session/token distribution. Please include per-request token counts and streaming-chunk markers if possible.

Measurement conventions we will include in the report
- E2E-first-byte: client-send -> first-byte (includes TLS + network + runtime first-token emission)
- E2E-last-byte: client-send -> last-byte (full response)
- Server-processing time: request-received -> last-byte-emit (server-side only)

Proposed Redwood test config (what we’ll stand up)
- hosted-small: baseline instance group (autoscaled) — target steady qps 20–60, concurrency cap 150
- hosted-boost: higher-end instance group — target steady qps 60–120, concurrency cap 400
- For streaming we’ll enable chunked-send with keep-alive and measure first-chunk latencies separately.

Instrumented headers we will require for correlation
- x-rw-testid: unique per test run
- x-rw-session: session id forwarded from your replay
- x-rw-client-ts: client-send timestamp (ms since epoch)

Proposed acceptance rules
- Baseline: Redwood-hosted must meet your p95/p99 targets on hosted-small or hosted-boost (we’ll show both).
- If hosted-small misses p99 but hosted-boost meets it, we’ll produce a sizing recommendation and cost delta.

Timeline reminder
- May 13: Acme provides sample and definitive SLO definition
- May 18: setup and endpoint details from Redwood
- May 19–21: PoC run window

I’ve attached the sample latency log format (redwood-hosted-latency-samples.jsonl) and updated the checklist spreadsheet.

— Soojin

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>

Subject: Re: Real-world latency checklist and verification plan (hosted vs current provider)

Adding a short technical acceptance checklist from the infra side — these are the concrete hooks we need in the replay and the PoC to make the results comparable and actionable.

Technical acceptance checklist (required)
- Correlation headers present for every request: x-rw-testid, x-rw-session, x-rw-client-ts. We’ll reject traces missing these.
- Sample size: for p99 stability, we need at least 100k completed requests in the aggregated window or a clear statistical adjustment if fewer samples; please indicate expected total request count for the replay.
- Measurement definitions: we will report both client-send->first-byte and client-send->last-byte. For p99 comparisons use client-send->first-byte unless you explicitly prefer last-byte.
- Error handling: classify and report 4xx/5xx, timeouts, and truncated streams separately. A run is considered failed if 5xx rate > 0.5% sustained.
- Network parity: run the same IP egress region for Redwood and for your current provider. If your incumbent uses an internal gateway, notify us so we can route accordingly.
- Streaming specifics: for multi-chunk flows, ensure the replay marks chunk boundaries; we’ll compute per-chunk first-byte metrics and inter-chunk jitter.

Optional but highly recommended
- Include TLS handshake timing if you can capture client-side metrics (helps separate network vs processing).
- If you use short-lived connections, let us know so we can emulate connection churn.

I attached a short acceptance-form template you can fill quickly (I’ll add an example of a filled file for the first test run).

Ben Carter
Principal SRE | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.inference.com

Attachments: redwood-hosted-latency-samples.jsonl (format example), poc-acceptance-template.csv
